adjudicated_text: अच्छा॑ म॒ इन्द्रं॑ म॒तयः॑ स्व॒र्विदः॑ स॒ध्रीची॒र्विश्वा॑ उश॒तीर॑नूषत । ॥ १७ ॥
adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 6 svarita = 12, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 12 marks (verified programmatically). T1 and T3 produced byte-identical text_devanagari. All three independently isolated the same difficult mark: a svarita at x~690 in INDRAM that MERGES with the anusvara dot into a single ink component at low threshold and separates only at a higher one (T3: merges at 140, separates at 170; T1 and T2 separated it by shape - stroke 10-12 x 37 px against dot 20-22 x 22 px, the dot matching this line's two visargas at 21 x 24 px). All three also noted that the line-attribution trap cannot fire here: line 9 opens a new hymn after extra leading, so line 8's bar band is TWO line-pitches away with ~189 completely blank rows between. Two loci were disputed, both resolved 2-1, neither affecting a mark tuple: (1) word 5 aksara 1: DHRI (T1, T3) vs DHI (T2). Adopted DHRI on the 2-1 majority. T2 argued from descender depth that no subscript RA is present; T3 recorded the glyph as its single unclear aksara (DHRA vs SHRA). The aksara CLUSTER COUNT is 5 either way, so the anudatta on aksara 2 and the svarita on aksara 4 are unaffected. T2's dissent is preserved. (2) terminal punctuation spacing: spaced (T1, T3) vs unspaced (T2). Adopted the spaced form on the 2-1 majority. NOTE this is NOT cosmetic: it changes the whitespace token count from 11 to 9 and therefore what the binder's token/span alignment guard sees. Reported explicitly rather than smoothed away.

readers.initial_text: अच्छा॑ म॒ इन्द्रं॑ म॒तयः॑ स्व॒र्विदः॑ स॒ध्रीची॒र्विश्वा॑ उश॒तीर॑नूषत । ॥ १७ ॥
readers.y_bands: All y values are leaf-block rows (block = 3226 x 5006, from find_text_block on canvas 411); line 9 itself is block y 1890-2011. Measured by full-width row-ink projection (threshold 128) plus connected-component extents. LINE-ABOVE (line 8) BAR BAND: y 1673-1694 (line 8 bodies end y~1660; its descender plateau y 1661-1672; its bars peak at 253 inked px in row 1681). CLEAN GUTTER: rows 1695-1883 carry ZERO inked pixels across all 3226 columns - line 9 opens a new hymn after a 189-row blank, so there is no line-above bar contamination anywhere in my upper gutter. MY SVARITA BAND: y 1883-1924 (stroke tops 1883-1886 on the left of the line, 1893-1895 on the right; each stroke foot merges into the sirorekha). MY SIROREKHA: top edge = 0.0047*x + 1918 (y 1918 at x=200 rising to y 1930 at x=2500; the whole line slopes down to the right by ~14 px over 3226 px), thickness ~17 px; peak headline rows y 1930-1934 (2100-2122 inked px per row). MY GLYPH BODY: y ~1936-2008 (baseline ~2003 at x=200, ~2013 at x=2600). MY DESCENDER PLATEAU (not accent): y 2009-2026, only 30-50 inked px per row - the foot of da in vidah, the uu hook of nuu, and stem serifs. MY OWN ANUDATTA BAR BAND: y 2027-2047; individual bars y 2027-2036 at x=507 drifting to y 2037-2047 at x=2211, following the same line slope; each bar 10-11 px tall and 37-39 px wide. LOWER GUTTER: rows 2048-2058 carry ZERO ink across all columns. NEXT LINE (line 10): its above-headline band starts y 2059; its sirorekha y 2094-2110; its body from y 2110. Because both gutters (1695-1883 above, 2048-2058 below) are completely blank, every mark I report is unambiguously inside line 9's own two accent bands.
readers.boundary_interpretation: WORD BOUNDARIES. I found them by projecting ink only inside a 19-row window that tracks the fitted sirorekha (y = 0.0047*x + 1918 .. +16) and taking runs of >=8 inked rows per column. The headline runs are: 182-406 | 446-529 | 571-726 | 764-985 | 1084-1379 | 1471-1584 + 1589-1743 + 1746-2032 | 2073-2597 | 2649-2664 (danda) | 2933-3184 (double danda, numeral, double danda). Inter-word headline gaps are 38-58 px (40, 42, 38, 58, 52, 41, 52). The two gaps of 5 px and 3 px inside 1471-2032 are ink breaks in a single 562-px-long headline, an order of magnitude below any real word gap, so 1471-2032 is ONE printed word (sadhriicii-rvishvaa). The two visargas (1007-1027 and 1398-1419) are free-standing dot pairs, not headline-joined; I attached each to the word on its left, whose headline ends 19-23 px earlier. That gives 7 text words, then the danda, then the flush-right numeral group. Word indices 0-6 are the text words; 7 = danda, 8 = first double danda, 9 = the numeral 17, 10 = closing double danda. AKSARA BOUNDARIES. Inside each word I segmented on a second projection taken 19-86 rows BELOW the fitted sirorekha, i.e. the glyph bodies only, where aksaras separate even though their headlines are joined. The body runs are: 184-277 | 285-366 | 377-393 || 453-523 || 578-721 || 768-838 | 854-907 | 924-981 | 1007-1027 || 1088-1191 | 1215-1232 | 1255-1309 | 1324-1378 | 1398-1419 || 1473-1542 | 1556-1614 | 1630-1649 | 1668-1734 | 1755-1772 | 1794-1811 | 1835-1891 | 1907-1983 | 2003-2021 || 2078-2144 | 2156-2226 | 2238-2291 | 2310-2329 | 2346-2452 | 2467-2520 | 2535-2589. CALIBRATION THAT RESOLVES THE NEAR-BOUNDARY MARKS. All six anudatta bars sit with their RIGHT edge within 2 px of the right edge of one glyph body: 525/523, 839/838, 1191/1191, 1543/1542, 1733/1734, 2230/2226. That is a fixed fount offset (the bar is cut under the right two thirds of the aksara), so each bar has exactly one candidate body and none of them is genuinely ambiguous. All six svarita strokes sit with their centre INSIDE one glyph body span: 327 in 285-366, 694 in 578-721, 964 in 924-981, 1358 in 1324-1378, 1970 in 1907-1983, 2366 in 2346-2393. INDIVIDUAL CALLS. (1) The bar at 821 in matayah looks as if it straddles ma/ta at band scale; it does not - it spans 802-839, ma's body is 768-838 and ta's body starts at 854, so it stops 15 px short of ta. Assigned to ma (aksara 0). (2) The bar at 1173 lies under the -va half of the s+va conjunct (body 1088-1191, two humps in the column profile). s and va are one aksara, so it is assigned to the conjunct sva (aksara 0), not to a separate va. (3) The bar at 1525 spans 1507-1543; sa's body is 1473-1542 and dhra's body starts at 1556, so it is sa (aksara 0), not dhrii. (4) The bar at 1715 spans 1697-1733; the ca body is 1668-1734 and its ii stem is 1755-1772, so it belongs to the aksara cii (aksara 2). (5) The svarita at 327 sits between a (body 184-277) and the aa stem (377-393); its centre is 2 px off the centre of the 285-366 body and it is 50 px clear of a's right edge, so it is on the c-cha-aa aksara (index 1), not on the initial a. (6) The svarita at 2366 falls inside the merged body run 2346-2452; the column profile and a 6x crop split that run into ra (2346-2393) and na (2393-2452, carrying the uu hook at 2412-2480). 2360-2371 is wholly inside ra, so it is assigned to ra (aksara 3), not to nuu. (7) The svarita at 694 in indram is 4 px from the anusvara dot and merges with it into one ink blob at every threshold; I separated them by shape - the stroke is x 689-698 by y 1883-1920 (10 wide, 37 tall) and the dot is x 698-720 by y 1899-1921 (22 by 22). The stroke is on the n-d-ra-anusvara cluster (aksara 1). (8) The svaritas at 964 and 1358 each sit over a body (ya 924-981, da 1324-1378) that is followed by a free-standing visarga; I read the visarga as part of the same aksara, so they are aksara 2 in both words.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION AND METHOD. I started from the two supplied 1568-px segment crops, then rendered my own slices of the same line at 2.7x, 4x, 6x, 7x, 10x and 20x of the native block pixels, binarised at thresholds 110/118/128/145. All positions and sizes are measured, not eyeballed: full-width row-ink projections, per-column ink profiles in a window that tracks the fitted sirorekha, and 8-connected component extents. I repeated the component analysis of both accent bands at thresholds 110, 128 and 145; the mark inventory is identical at all three (6 flat bars, 6 upright strokes) and only the measured widths move by 1-2 px. THE SIX ANUDATTA. Centres 507, 821, 1173, 1525, 1715, 2211; extents (thr 128) 489-525, 802-839, 1155-1191, 1507-1543, 1697-1733, 2192-2230; each 37-39 px wide and 10-11 px tall, all inside y 2027-2047, all with clear white above them and 11+ rows of white below the band. Distinctly wider than tall, as the print specifies. THE SIX SVARITA. Centres 327, 694, 964, 1358, 1970, 2366; extents 322-332, 689-698, 958-969, 1352-1363, 1964-1976, 2360-2371; each 9-15 px wide and 28-37 px tall, tops at y 1883-1895, standing clear above the sirorekha. Distinctly taller than wide. FALSE POSITIVES I REJECTED, BY SHAPE. (a) uu-matra hook of nuu at x 2412-2480, y 2014-2046: 69 px wide, 33 px tall, a curved hook running straight out of the na body - three times the height of a bar; rejected. (b) Foot of da in vidah at x 1374-1387, y 2014-2021: 14 px wide and continuous with the da body above it, so neither isolated nor bar-shaped; rejected. (c) Subscript ra (ra-phala) diagonals under d-ra in indram (~x 700-727), under dh-ra in dhrii (~x 1590-1614), the tail of half-sa in sva (~x 1100-1150) and the tail of the initial i: all slanted strokes joined to their own glyph bodies, none a free flat dash. (d) Six wide curved shapes above the headline, which are the trap for svarita: x 1216-1301 (i-matra curl plus repha of -rvi- in svarvidah, 84 px across), 1591-1644 (ii of dhrii, 54), 1715-1770 (ii of cii, 55), 1794-1840 (i of -rvi-, 46), 1844-1883 (the repha itself, 40), 2271-2326 (ii of tii, 56). Each is 39-86 px wide with 0.54-0.72 fill and, at 9-12x, resolves into loops or hooks; I opened every one of them and confirmed there is no narrow upright stroke hidden inside. Real svarita on this line are 9-15 px wide. (e) Two visargas, x 1007-1027 (yah) and 1398-1419 (dah): each two round dots about 21 wide by 24 tall stacked across the body band, not upright strokes. (f) One anusvara, x 698-720, y 1899-1921, 22 by 22 - as wide as tall, and it merges into the same ink blob as the indram svarita; separated by shape as described in boundary_interpretation. (g) The danda at x 2649-2666 and the four danda strokes of the numeral group (2933-2952, 2956-2974, 3146-3162, 3164-3184) are 16-21 px wide and 71-74 tall and stop at y ~2013; they never reach the bar band, so no danda slice was mistaken for a mark. (h) Line 8's own bar band, y 1673-1694, is 189 completely blank rows above my svarita band - I verified zero inked pixels in rows 1695-1883 across all 3226 columns - so on this particular line the line-attribution trap does not bite at all. Line 9 is the indented opening line of a new hymn and sits after an unusually large 229-row vertical break. READING DIFFICULTIES. (1) Word 0 aksara 1 was the only glyph I had to argue about. It is 82 px wide (285-366) with THREE enclosed counters (x 301-314, 329-338, 308-331) and a descending tail at 345-367. Its column profile shows TWO humps before the final stem, exactly like the known conjuncts s-va (104 px, two humps) and sh-va (77 px, two humps), and unlike the single consonants on this same line - ca is 67 px with ONE hump and ONE counter, sha is 71 px with one hump plus a thin connector and ONE counter. Every single-consonant body on this line measures 47-71 px. So the ink says this is a two-consonant conjunct carrying aa, and I read it as c-cha-aa. A reader who read it as a bare chha would still put the svarita on the same aksara, so the accent record is unaffected either way. I template-matched this glyph against the whole leaf; it does not recur (best non-self Jaccard 0.70, i.e. background), so no further internal evidence was available. I followed the fount note and read the first glyph, which looks like vocalic r or shra, as a. (2) The numeral. I built a numeral inventory from the other numerals printed on this same leaf: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 0 all occur here. Line 9's first digit is the loop-plus-straight-stem form that appears alone as 1 elsewhere on the leaf; its second digit (x 3058-3121) is the ring with a teardrop counter at upper right and a hook leaving at mid left, which matches the 7 printed on line 22 and is clearly not the 9 on line 2 (counter upper left, tail sweeping to lower right) nor the open 3 on line 14. So I read the numeral as 17. Note that it is NOT a running verse number on this page: the preceding line ends 12 and the following lines run 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, so the flush-right 17 on line 9 behaves like the number of the hymn that line 9 opens. I recorded the digits as printed and did not adjust them. (3) Nothing else was left unresolved, so unclear_count is 0. I consulted no text, edition, translation, database or web resource, and I did not read the detector scripts, the transcription directory, or any other reader's work.

readers.boundary_interpretation: WORD BOUNDARIES: from breaks in the sirorekha, measured as gaps between the x-extents of the headline-joined connected components. Seven clusters: 182-407, 446-530, 570-728, 763-1028 (incl. visarga 1007-1028), 1083-1421 (incl. visarga 1399-1421), 1471-2033, 2072-2598; then the danda at 2649-2667 and the sign group 2933-3185. The six inter-word gaps are 39, 40, 35, 55, 50 and 39 px - far wider than the largest within-word headline nick (13 px, between अ and च्छा at 274-285, and 2 px between म and त of मतयः at 845-847), so the word split is unambiguous. AKSARA BOUNDARIES: from the column-ink profile of the body zone only (from headline_top+22 down to y 2005), which isolates each consonant's stem block. Body runs: अ 184-274 | च्छ 285-367 + aa-matra 377-394 || म 453-524 || इ 579-640, न्द्र 640-722 || म 769-839, त 854-907, य 925-981 || स्व 1088-1192, र्वि 1255-1310, द 1325-1376 || स 1473-1542, ध 1558-1615 + ii-stem 1630-1650, च 1668-1735 + ii-stem 1755-1773, र्वि 1794-1891, श्व 1909-1983 + aa 2004-2022 || उ 2078-2145, श 2158-2227, त 2238-2291 + ii-stem 2311-2330, र 2346-2383, न 2387-2452, ष 2468-2521, त 2535-2589. PLACEMENT RULE, calibrated on the uncontested marks and then applied to the contested ones: this fount sets the anudatta bar under the RIGHT PORTION of its aksara, with the bar's right edge flush (+/-6 px) with the right edge of that aksara's consonant body, and sets the svarita stroke 13-29 px LEFT of that same right edge. Calibrated on the isolated one-aksara word म (word 1): body 453-524, bar 488-527, delta +3. MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY, and the side I assigned each to: (1) bar at 821 (span 801-841), between म (769-839) and त (854-907) of मतयः - assigned to म: the bar lies wholly inside म's span, its right edge 841 is flush with म's 839, and it does not reach त. (2) bar at 1173 (span 1154-1193), between स्व (1088-1192) and र्वि (1255-1310) of स्वर्विदः - assigned to स्व: right edges 1193 vs 1192, flush; the 1192-1216 body gap lies to its right. (3) bar at 1716 (span 1696-1736), between the च of ची (1668-1735) and that aksara's own ii-stem (1755-1773) - assigned to ची: right edges 1736 vs 1735, flush, and the ii-matra belongs to the same aksara, so nothing crosses an aksara boundary. (4) bar at 2211 (span 2191-2232), between श (2158-2227) and ती (2238-2291) of उशतीरनूषत - assigned to श: right edge 2232 is flush with श's 2227 and stops 6 px short of त's left edge 2238. (5) stroke at 2366 (span 2359-2374), sitting over the र/न junction of ...तीरनूषत where there is a visible 4 px headline nick at 2383-2387 - assigned to र: the stroke is entirely inside र's body span 2346-2383, 17 px left of र's right edge, matching the svarita offset measured on the uncontested strokes (य 22, दः 18, श्वा 13); न starts 13 px right of the stroke. (6) stroke at 1970 (span 1962-1979) - assigned to श्वा (body 1909-1983), not to र्वि: it is 79 px right of र्वि's व (ends 1891) and 13 px left of श्व's right edge. (7) stroke at 693 (span 686-700) in इन्द्रं - the one mark that touches another mark: at threshold 128 it labels as a single blob 688-720. A pixel map shows two elements fusing only at y~1900: a 12 px wide upright x 687-698 running y 1882-1918, and a round blob x 702-722 / y 1897-1919 measuring 20x22. This line's two visargas measure 21x24 and 21x24, so the round blob is a printed dot - the anusvara of इन्द्रं - and only the left element is the svarita. Assigned to the aksara न्द्रं, which carries both. (8) stroke at 327 in अच्छा - the only within-word headline break there is at 274-285, between अ and च्छा; the stroke at 322-333 is 48 px right of that break and centred over the च्छ bowl, so it is on च्छा, not on अ.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION AND METHOD. (a) Read the two supplied 2-segment crops. (b) Re-rendered the same line with scripts/crop_atharvaveda_line.py 411 --line 9 --segments 4. (c) Measured the source raster directly with PIL/numpy on the leaf text block (crop 412,382-3638,5388 of bsb10219750_00411.jpg, 4000x5900): full-width row-ink projections at thresholds 110/128/145/160/175; a per-column sirorekha-top locator (41 px horizontal run test) which measured the page skew as +11 px over 2300 px; skew-corrected connected-component extraction in the above-headline band and in the below-body band; per-word column-ink profiles of the body zone; and raw pixel maps. (d) Rendered my own 5x-12x zooms of every word and every candidate mark - plain, autocontrast-sharpened, and binarised. STABILITY. The mark set is identical at thresholds 110, 128, 145, 160 and 175. In the bar band there are exactly six components, w 37-42 px, h 10-15 px (h/w 0.26-0.36, distinctly wider than tall). Above the headline there are exactly six narrow uprights, w 11-17 px, h 30-36 px (h/w 2.0-2.8). The two populations do not overlap on any measure, and the six of each kind are near-identical in size, as type-set marks should be. FALSE POSITIVES REJECTED, BY SHAPE. (1) x 2411-2483, y 2008-2049 (w 71, h 41): a curved hook running continuously up into the न of नूषत - the u/uu-matra of नू, not a dash; the only thing in the gutter taller than 15 px. (2) x 1365-1389, y 2008-2023 (w 24, h 15): the curved tail of the द of विदः - above the bar band and curved, not a flat dash. (3) Four stubs confined to y 2008-2015 (x 634-646, 2381-2396, 3030-3048, 3072-3104): bottoms of descenders, the danda and the numerals leaking into the band, each connecting upward into its glyph with no white gap. (4) Above the headline, five wide curved shapes, w 56-104 px, h/w 0.26-0.55: x 1589-1662 (ii-matra of धी), 1700-1778 (ii-matra of ची), 1790-1928 (i-matra plus repha of र्वि in चीर्विश्वा), 1212-1305 (i-matra plus repha of र्वि in स्वर्विदः), 2217-2334 (ii-matra of ती) - matras and repha, not narrow strokes. (5) The round dot x 702-722 above इन्द्रं: anusvara, 20x22, as wide as tall, sized exactly like this line's visarga dots (21x24). (6) x 2941-2956 and 3009-3032, y 1911-1929: tops of the double danda and of the numeral १, not free-standing strokes. (7) No danda or double-danda slice crosses either band - the single danda 2649-2667 and the sign group 2933-3185 both stop above y 2020. (8) The 2-5 px high slivers that appear only at threshold 175 (x 453-512, 573-624, 774-809, 842-955, 1474-1510, 2001-2028, 2078-2126, 2139-2208, 2539-2564) are the fuzzy upper edge of my own sirorekha. (9) No vocalic-ri hook is present anywhere in the gutter of this line: nothing in the bar band exceeds 15 px in height, and the 21-33 px curved hooks the brief warns about are simply absent here. NO LINE-ABOVE CONTAMINATION. On this line the classic trap cannot fire: lines 8 and 9 are two pitches apart and y 1695-1883 is completely blank, so line 8's bar band (1673-1694) lies 332 px above mine (2026-2050). I checked the converse too - line 10's upper matra band starts at y 2059, nine blank rows below my bar band's floor, and all six of my bars sit at 2026-2049 carrying MY sirorekha's skew, not line 10's. READINGS I HAD TO SETTLE FROM THE INK. (i) Word 5, aksara 1: I read धी, not ध्री. The glyph's ink bottoms at y 2003, the same as this line's plain consonants (च 2003, स 2004, त 2005, श 2007), whereas the one certain subscript-ra on the line - the द्र of इन्द्रं - reaches y 2012 and shows its subscript as a separate descending diagonal. No such diagonal exists under this ध at any threshold. My memory of the Rigvedic parallel suggested a -dhri- form; the ink does not support a subscript ra here, so I followed the ink and print सधीचीर्विश्वा. (ii) The verse sign is a single danda, then a ~265 px gap, then ॥ १ ७ ॥: the first numeral has a closed upper bowl with a straight vertical descender on its right (१); the second is an all-curl closed loop entered by a hook from the lower left with no straight descender (७). Read as ॥१७॥. (iii) The word-initial glyph of word 0 is the fount's अ, which looks like ऋ or श्र; read as अ per the established fount note. UNRESOLVED (unclear_count = 1). Word 0, aksara 1: the 82 px bowl-form conjunct I transcribe च्छा. Its width places it firmly in this line's conjunct class (न्द्र 82, स्व 104) and outside the single-consonant class (त 53, ष 53, य 56, च 67, श 69, स 69, म 70-71), and it carries a short lower-right subscript diagonal reaching y 2003, so it is certainly a conjunct plus aa-matra; but at 2024 px the individual half-consonant inside the bowl is not separately resolvable, so I could not read the first member from its shape alone. This does not affect the accent record: the svarita at x 327 sits over that aksara whatever its identity, and its aksara index (1) is fixed by the अ/च्छा headline break at 274-285. CONFIDENCE. High on the accent layer, on two independent internal checks: both accent bands carry my own sirorekha's skew (so all twelve marks are line 9's), and the placement rule derived from the isolated one-aksara word म (bar right edge flush with the aksara body's right edge; svarita 13-29 px left of it) holds for all twelve marks with no exception.

Aksara indices count graphic clusters, with matra, visarga and a preceding repha folded into the cluster they are drawn on: accha = [a][cchaa]; ma = [ma]; indram = [i][ndram]; matayah = [ma][ta][yah]; svarvidah = [sva][rvi][dah]; sadhriiciirvishvaa = [sa][dhrii][cii][rvi][shvaa]; ushatiiranuushata = [u][sha][tii][ra][nuu][sha][ta]. Marks near a boundary, and how each was decided. All six bars lie wholly inside one body-band run, and this print sets a bar under the RIGHT part of its aksara with the bar's right edge flush to the aksara's right edge - a rule that held for all six without exception. (1) x820 in matayah: bar spans 801-839, ma spans 768-840, ta starts at 854. The centre is 34 px inside ma, the right edge 1 px inside ma's, and the bar does not overlap ta at all -> ma, not ta. The isolated one-letter word ma at 453-525 carries its bar at 488-525, the same 72-79% offset, which is what establishes the rule. (2) x1525 in sadhriiciirvishvaa: bar 1507-1543, sa 1472-1542, next element starts 1555; right edge 1 px past sa's, still 12 px clear of the next -> sa. (3) x2211 in ushatiiranuushata: bar 2192-2230, sha 2155-2226, ta starts 2238; right edge 4 px past sha's, 8 px clear of ta -> sha. (4) x1716: bar 1697-1734 under ca 1668-1735; the preceding cluster dhrii ends at 1650 and 1651-1667 is empty -> cii, not dhrii. (5) x1173: falls under the subscript va of the sva conjunct (single run 1087-1203), one aksara, so index 0 either way. All six svaritas fall wholly within a single body-band run's x-span - four of them right-of-centre over it, two effectively centred - and none is within 10 px of a run boundary, so no svarita required a side decision. The only orthographic (not spatial) call is the repha in -rvi-: ra+virama is drawn above the headline, and I count it with the following vi as the graphic cluster [rvi], which is why svarvidah has 3 aksaras and not 4. No accent mark sits on a repha, so this choice moves no carrier.
readers.notes: Method. I worked from the source scan, not from the supplied crops alone: leaf bsb10219750_00411.jpg, text block (412,382)-(3638,5388) = 3226x5006, line 9 at block y1890-2011. Global line-x equals block-x (seg1_x/0.9440 inverts to block-x exactly), so every x reported is directly comparable. Measurement was by PIL row and column ink profiles and 8-connected component extents at thresholds 140, 170 and 190, plus my own crops rendered at 2.4x-15.7x of the native raster (the 4000 px file is an upscale of a 2024 px master, so this is magnification, not extra detail). I deskewed by a 0.00616 px/px shear before banding; that sharpened the sirorekha and put all six bars at one identical deskewed y-centre of 2028.4 - independent confirmation that they are one line's bar row and not a mixture of two lines'. ANUDATTA: 6 found, every one isolated and inside my own bar band, 37-39 px wide by 10-13 px tall (aspect 3.0-3.8), centres x507, 820, 1173, 1525, 1716, 2211. The row-ink budget agrees: peak 269 px in the bar band minus the ~50 px descender floor leaves ~219 px, i.e. six bars of ~38 px with no room for a seventh. SVARITA: 6 found, isolated upright strokes standing clear above the sirorekha, 11-17 px wide by >=29 px tall (aspect 0.38-0.50), centres x327, 694, 963, 1357, 1970, 2366. Rejected false positives, by shape. (a) Six wide curved shapes above the headline: x1216-1301 (86 px, repha plus i-matra of -rvi- in svarvidah, two merged hooks), x1590-1646 (57 px, ii-matra of dhrii), x1714-1773 (60 px, ii-matra of cii), x1795-1841 (47 px, repha) and x1843-1887 (45 px, i-matra of vi) in -rvishvaa, x2270-2327 (58 px, ii-matra of tii). All are hooks or crescents in the 50-68 px matra class, or two such merged, not narrow uprights. (b) One round dot, x703-720 in indram, about 16x16 and sitting lower than its neighbour: anusvara, not svarita. The stroke beside it at x686-702 IS a svarita; the two are separate blobs that only merge at threshold 140, and the stroke tops out 13 rows higher. (c) In the bar band, component x2412-2480 (deskewed y2014-2031, aspect 1.5-2.1) is the uu-matra of nuu in ushatiiranuushata: a curved hook running continuously up into the body with no white gap, so not a bar. (d) Thin diagonal terminal flicks under cha, i, sa, sha and da (attached, diagonal, 25-35 px long, in the descender zone y1995-2020) - the halanta-tail class; none is a horizontal dash and none reaches the bar band. (e) A 3x4 px speck at x3049, y1758-1761 in the empty gutter: noise, far too small for either mark. (f) Nothing accentual right of x2366 - the danda at 2649-2666, the double dandas and the numerals carry nothing above or below them. Unresolved. One cluster, the second aksara of word 5 (body-band run 1555-1615 plus its subscript wedge): I read it as dha + subscript ra = dhrii, but at this raster I cannot fully exclude shri, so I have counted it in unclear_count. It carries no accent mark, so it cannot move any carrier. A lesser doubt I did not count: the second verse numeral (x3058-3122) is a bold loop with a tail curling to the bottom-left, which I read as 7, giving 17; it is clearly not a 9 (no straight right descender) and not a 0. For the record, word 1 is a bare single letter ma carrying an anudatta - unusual as a word, but the ink shows one glyph at 453-525 with nothing above the headline and no matra, so that is what I recorded rather than smoothing it to me or maa. The first glyph of the line was read as a per the fount note; it does look like vocalic r to a modern eye.
